# Golden Pipeline Template — the ideal output of every workflow stage

This directory is a **hand-built reference** showing what a *good* run of the DeepResearchForecast /
MiroFish pipeline should produce **at each stage**. It was authored by Claude as a quality bar — it was
**not** generated by a live MiniMax pipeline run. The live AI workflow (and any human reviewing it) can
consult these files to see the target shape, richness, and internal consistency to aim for.

> **Topic (illustrative):** Data-center AI accelerator market through end-2027.
> **Central question:** By 31 Dec 2027, will NVIDIA retain ≥75% revenue share of the data-center AI
> accelerator (training+inference silicon) market, or will hyperscaler custom ASICs (Google TPU, AWS
> Trainium, Microsoft Maia, Meta MTIA) plus AMD Instinct erode NVIDIA below 75%?
> The numbers and relationships are realistic-but-illustrative, chosen to exercise every field of the
> contract — not freshly-researched live facts.

## Why this exists

A real run is large: dozens of actors, a dense typed relationship graph, a ~100-node knowledge graph, 80
personas, a 40-round dual-platform simulation, and a 7-section report. It is easy for a stage to under-
produce (a 12-node graph, generic personas, untyped edges, dropped actor motivations). This template
pins the **ideal**: fully-populated schemas, rich character interiors, an accurately-typed and densely-
connected graph, and faithful flow of the researched signal all the way to the report.

## The pipeline and which file is the ideal output of each stage

```
 deep research        →  structured extraction        →  ontology  →  knowledge graph  →  personas  →  simulation  →  report
 dossier.md              actors.json                      ontology.json graph.json          personas.json forum.json    report.md
 research_log.txt        sources.json                                                                                   
                         quantitative.json
                         contested.json
```

| Stage | File(s) | What the template demonstrates (the bar to hit) |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Deep research** | `dossier.md`, `research_log.txt` | Decision-grade dossier per the deep-research SKILL §12 contract: thesis + calibrated probability, layered claims (known/inferred/assumed/unknown), situation brief, **actor & incentives**, a **directed typed relationship table**, drivers & watch-indicators, base/upside/downside scenarios, key-assumptions + premortem, inline tiered source attributions. `research_log.txt` shows the KIQ→search→tier→triangulate→synthesis-gate methodology. |
| **2. Structured extraction** | `actors.json` | The **single source of truth / handoff contract**. 34 actors, each with the *enhanced* schema: `description` (one disambiguating sentence) · `aliases` (incl. foreign-language, for zero-overlap resolution) · `goals`/`constraints`/`assets`/`vulnerabilities` · `stated_vs_revealed` · `grade` (Admiralty) · `role`/`stance`/`influence`/`memory`. Plus `situation_brief`, 16 `key_events`, 12 `hot_topics`, and **77 typed `relationships`** (`ALLY_OF`/`OPPOSES`/`COMPETES_WITH`/`REGULATES`/`DEPENDS_ON`/`PARTNERS_WITH`/`INFLUENCES`/`OTHER`+`relation_label`) each with `sign`/`strength`/`grade`/`basis` (some `since`/`until`). Every relationship endpoint resolves to a named actor. |
| | `sources.json` | 35 sources, **tiered S1–S4** with `date`, `supports`, `independent` — provenance preserved, not just URLs. |
| | `quantitative.json` | 26 load-bearing numbers, each with `unit` + `as_of_date` + `definition` (guards definition-drift). |
| | `contested.json` | 9 genuine evidence conflicts: the disputed claim, the differing positions with their sources/tiers, status, and **why they differ**. |
| **3. Ontology** | `ontology.json` | Domain-adaptive (`general_forecast`) ontology that *fits this domain* — 10 entity types (ChipVendor, Foundry, MemoryMaker, Hyperscaler, CustomSiliconPartner, AILab, Neocloud, …) with behaviour-driving attributes (role, stance, influence_tier, market_share, motivation); 10 edge types reusing the researched relationship taxonomy + domain edges (SUPPLIES/CO_DESIGNS), with edge attributes (sentiment/strength/since_date/basis). |
| **4. Knowledge graph** | `graph.json` | A **large** KG (103 nodes, 206 links) — the antithesis of a 12-node toy. Nodes for all 34 actors (typed labels + grounded one-sentence `summary` per the KG-cookbook description-for-disambiguation rule), ~33 technology/market concept nodes, 16 event nodes, and 8 alias nodes. Links: every researched relationship (sign/strength folded into `fact`), `IS_A`, `ALSO_KNOWN_AS` alias bridges, actor→concept `DEPENDS_ON`/`USES`/`INFLUENCES`, and ~25 simulation-derived edges (`FOLLOWED`/`REPLIED_TO`/`QUOTED`/`LIKED`, fact ending `(round N)`). **0 dangling links.** Format matches real output: `{nodes:[{id,name,labels,summary}], links:[{source,target,name,fact}], graph_id}`. |
| **5. Prepare / personas** | `personas.json` | 24 OASIS agent profiles grounded in the actors: bio/persona seeded from the actor's role/stance/goals/motivation, naming real counterparts from the relationship graph as their social network, with influence-scaled follower/karma. Includes a note that a **live run expands to 80** by adding ~55 synthetic audience personas sampled around these anchors. |
| **6. Simulation** | `forum.json` | A sample dual-platform (Twitter/Reddit) transcript: in-character posts + replies debating the central question, chip vendors vs hyperscalers vs analysts vs a regulator voice. Note: a live run is **40 rounds / 80 agents**; this is a 3-round excerpt showing the shape. |
| **7. Report** | `report.md` | The final 7-section ReAct report: executive summary + headline probability, landscape, actor positions, **knowledge-graph relationship analysis with edge-citations** (e.g. `（依据：NVIDIA --[DEPENDS_ON]--> TSMC）`), simulation findings, scenarios with probabilities, drivers/indicators/risks. Calibrated language and `[S]` source tags throughout. |

## How to use it

- **As a quality bar / few-shot reference.** When a live stage produces an artifact, compare against the
  corresponding file here: is the graph this dense and typed? do personas carry researched motivation and a
  named social network? does the report cite graph edges? are actor `description`/`aliases` populated so KG
  resolution can merge zero-overlap aliases?
- **As a schema reference.** Every file matches the real pipeline artifact format, so it doubles as a
  worked example of the contract each stage must emit/consume. The `actors.json` ↔ `graph.json` ↔
  `personas.json` chain shows the *same cast* flowing through with consistent names + aliases.
- **It is not a fixture for tests** and not a published demo — it is internal guidance. Regenerate or
  extend it by hand (or with Claude, not the MiniMax pipeline) when the contract evolves.

## Internal-consistency guarantees (verified at build time)

- All 77 relationship endpoints resolve to a named actor (or alias).
- All 34 actors appear as nodes in `graph.json`; **0 dangling graph links**.
- Personas, forum participants, ontology types, and report citations all draw from the same actor cast.

See `meta.json` for exact counts and the stage→file map in machine-readable form.
